About Black Forest Labs
We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world.
Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use.
Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next.
 
Why This Role
We develop AI models and run the infrastructure on which those models are trained, deployed, and served to customers. Securing that infrastructure comes with real challenges: researchers need flexible access to significant compute resources, production systems need strong isolation and reliability, and model assets and customer data need protection throughout their lifecycle.
Our research and production infrastructure teams design, build, and operate these systems. We're looking for an experienced, hands-on security engineer to partner with them as we grow: someone who can dig into the details, do the engineering, and work alongside those teams to improve our defensive posture.
This is an engineering role: you'll spend time reading code, understanding systems, debugging problems, and shipping changes.
 
What You’ll Work On
These are the areas this role draws from; you're not expected to cover
them all at once:
• 
Infrastructure architecture and isolation. Understand how our research and production environments fit together, identify consequential attack paths, and work with infrastructure teams to improve network boundaries, workload isolation, and access controls.
• 
Identity and access. Improve how people, services, and workloads authenticate and obtain access to infrastructure. Reduce unnecessary privileges, strengthen secrets management, and develop practical approaches to short-lived credentials and privileged access.
• 
Cloud and compute security. Strengthen security across cloud infrastructure, compute clusters, containers, storage, and orchestration systems. Help establish reusable patterns that engineers can adopt without unnecessary friction.
• 
Model and customer-data protection. Work with research and engineering teams to protect model artifacts, training and inference pipelines, and sensitive data. Understand where trust boundaries matter and develop ways to verify that they hold.
• 
Security in engineering workflows. Improve the security of infrastructure-as-code, build and deployment pipelines, and software artifacts. Build tooling and guardrails that help engineering teams prevent, detect, and fix problems without making security a bottleneck.
What We’re Looking For
• 
Strong experience securing production cloud infrastructure, with a solid understanding of identity, networking, operating systems, and distributed systems.
• 
Hands-on engineering ability. You can write and review code, work with infrastructure-as-code, debug unfamiliar systems, and implement the improvements you recommend.
• 
Good security judgment. You can distinguish meaningful risks from theoretical ones, make sensible tradeoffs, and explain why a particular security improvement matters.
• 
Experience working closely with infrastructure or platform engineers, including designing changes that are practical to deploy and operate.
• 
Experience in using LLMs and agents for security work, along with a clear-eyed view of where they help, where they don't, and how they themselves can be attacked.
• 
Comfort working with real autonomy, finding your way through complex systems, and turning loosely defined problems into concrete improvements.
Experience with GPU clusters, ML infrastructure, multi-tenant services, Kubernetes, and software supply-chain security would be particularly relevant, but none is a prerequisite. We're more interested in people who have solved difficult security problems in real systems than in candidates who can check every box on a technology list.
 
How We Work Together
We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. This role is based in San Francisco, and you’ll join us in the office at least 2 days a week, or one full week every other week.
Everything we do is grounded in four values:
• 
Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.
• 
Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.
• 
Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.
• 
Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.
If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, we’d love to hear from you.

From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.

Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.

Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.

But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People > Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. About Us
Hozah is a tech-led, award-winning company driving change in the parking industry and reimagining urban mobility. Our mission is simple but powerful: to transform parking into a seamless, automated experience, paving the way for smarter, more sustainable cities.
With recent recognition as PayTech Company of the Year, a place among Deloitte’s Top 50 Fastest Growing Tech Companies in the UK, and significant VC/PE investment, we’re one of the fastest scaling companies in the country.

Role Overview
You will build the products drivers and car park operators use every day: ANPR camera enforcement, pay-by-web, Autopay, permits, a client console and a motorist account app, across about 160 sites, and the new products we build next. We are a small engineering team, and we form teams around the work from the people we have.
We work in Kotlin on the backend (Spring Boot WebFlux, a domain-driven layering of domain, edge services and repository, Postgres, Axon event sourcing and Pub/Sub) and in TypeScript with Next.js and React on the front end, on GCP and Kubernetes. You do not need to know Kotlin to apply. Our engineers work with AI coding agents day to day, and we are looking for people who use them well and check what they produce.
Every engineer here is product-minded. You will talk to the people who use what you build, decide with product people what is worth building, and find out afterwards whether it worked.
You will report to the CTO and work with a team that reviews each other’s work.

The Senior level
Senior Software Engineer. You own a product area: its architecture, how it is staged, its quality bar, and working out with customers what is needed. You may be the only engineer on a new product area, so you need to be able to work alone for weeks at a time and keep quality high without a peer reviewer. Other engineers will come to you for design review. 

Key Responsibilities
• 
Own the delivery of what you are given, from the first ticket to production, with tests, and be the person who fixes it if it breaks.
• 
Talk to the people who use what you build, and use what you learn to shape and cut scope.
• 
Write acceptance criteria, and check a feature after release to see whether it was used and whether it worked.
• 
Work in our existing codebase and its layering, and keep it consistent for the next engineer.
• 
Use AI coding agents as part of how you work, and be accountable for everything you ship, however it was written.
• 
Take part in the on-call rota and look after what you ship.
• 
Review other engineers’ pull requests, and welcome review of your own.
• 
Own the architecture and staging of a product area, and the quality bar for it.
• 
Work out with customers what is needed, and give design review to other engineers.

Who we’re looking for
• 
You’re product-minded. In the last 12 months you’ve talked to real users or customers, and what you learned changed or cut the scope of what you built. You write acceptance criteria, you check a feature after release, and you can say whether something you shipped got used.
• 
You’ve shipped production code end to end in the last 12 months, in any language. You can say what you personally built, and what happened after it went live.
• 
You test as you build. You can describe a bug you shipped and the test that would have caught it.
• 
You use AI coding agents in real work today, and you can describe how you check what they produce, including a time one was wrong.
• 
You’re willing to be on call, and you take ownership of what you ship. You don’t need to have been on call before.
• 
You work well in an existing codebase with a layered or domain-driven structure that you did not design, and you read before you write.
• 
You’re comfortable across the stack. You’ve changed a React or Next.js front end, or worked properly against an API contract, even if you lean backend.
• 
You review others’ pull requests, finding real problems and saying so well, and you change your own design when review shows you a better way.
• 
You’ve owned a product area on your own, from first design to production, and staged it so each stage delivered something usable.
• 
Ideally, you’ve modelled a domain in which the rules change over time (such as pricing, eligibility, tax or regulation) and can answer “what was true on a given date”.
• 
You’ve kept quality high without a peer reviewer, and other engineers have come to you for design review.
You do not need a degree, a particular programming language, or Kotlin. Experience of Axon, Temporal, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, parking or payments is welcome, but none of it is required.

Fully remote working in the UK if you want it, with our London office next to East Croydon Station available to you.

Real ownership: mid-level engineers own whole features, and senior engineers own a product area.

A team that works with AI coding agents every day and measures what they do for us.

A strong, high performing culture, with genuine influence over how that culture develops as Hozah grows.

A fully refurbished, modern office, right next to East Croydon Station (with a fully stocked kitchen, offering free breakfast, lunch and drinks!).
